newsitem.title: USA: Mason Oil sees initial drilling upping EPS.
newsitem.headline: Mason Oil sees initial drilling upping EPS.

text.p: Mason Oil Co Inc said Tuesday it estimates that based upon the successful completion of the company's initial drilling plans in Officer Basin in South Australia, earnings per share could reach 22 cents in fiscal 1998.

The company said that its chief geologist, John Naylor, was clearing arrangements with the Australian customs and immigrations authorities concerning its plans to drill three wells in Officer Basin "by as early as May."
At the same time, the company announced it was in the final stages of completing and securing a turnkey drilling contract with the Philippine National Oil Co (PNOC).
It said Naylor expects to complete and sign a final drilling contract with PNOC within the next several weeks.

Paul Ingram, Mason Oil's president, said that studies initiated by the Australian government's minerals division, MESA, estimated the reserve potential for the Officer Basin to be as high as 1.8 billion barrels of oil and/or five trillion cubic feet of gas.
Mason Oil Co. Inc. is an oil and gas exploration company with lease interest in South Australia.
